title: Anchor (level) definition
$comment: PLC-05: `slots` moved out of `required` because free placement (PLC-01) deletes it, and `max_emplacements` was added as the replacement denominator for the board-saturation invariant (validate_data.py) -- but at least one of the two must be present, or there is nothing to bound emplacement count against at all. That is what the `anyOf` below enforces at the schema layer, so an anchor authored with neither is rejected before validate_data.py's own semantic check ever runs.

capacity_mw.description: fixed. raised only by story beats.

paths.description: One or more lanes. WAR-01: a lane is addressed everywhere in the rules by its integer INDEX into this array (stable, orderable, identical in both languages) -- `id` is for authoring, dialog and the HUD only and is never compared by a rule. A single-lane anchor is `paths` with exactly one entry; that is the degenerate case the migration guarantees grades byte-identically to the old single-`path` shape.

items.description: [x, y] or [x, y, z]. z is the elevation LEVEL (an index, never pixels or a world height -- see PRD-THEATRE-SCALE.md 2.3), defaults to 0, and is not read by any rule yet -- TER-01 is what will read it.

slots.description: Fixed build points, as tile-CENTRE coordinates in the convention `Sim._placement_reason()` pins: a board `w` tiles wide has interior `[-0.5, w-0.5]`, so tile (0,0)'s centre is `[0, 0]`. Optional now (PLC-05): free placement (PLC-01) authors an anchor with no `slots` array at all, relying on `max_emplacements` as the emplacement-count cap instead. An anchor that DOES author `slots` may still omit `max_emplacements`; validate_data.py then falls back to len(slots), reproducing today's numbers exactly. LF-219: coordinates are `number`, not `integer` -- both rule engines have modelled position continuously since PLC-01 (`sim/content.py` loads these through `float()`, `Sim._placement_reason()` accepts any float), and PLC-04's candidate lattice works at half-tile pitch, so the schema was the ONLY thing forcing authored slots onto the integer grid. It said so wrongly for long enough that the LF-185 re-siting pass searched integer positions only. `minimum: 0` stays: it is looser than the real bound (a footprint of radius 0.45 needs `x >= -0.05`), and validate_data.py applies the engines' own footprint-aware bounds and lane-standoff predicate on top.

max_emplacements.description: Hard cap on emplacements built at once -- the board-saturation invariant's denominator (validate_data.py compares capacity_mw against max_emplacements * max_draw, the same shape as the old len(slots) * max_draw). Required when `slots` is absent (see the root `anyOf`); optional when `slots` is present, in which case validate_data.py uses len(slots) as before. Chosen over the two rejected alternatives -- buildable-area/footprint (a looser upper bound the player can never reach, kept as a second WARNING-only check) and funds (rejected for circularity: bounties depend on kills, kills depend on the build) -- because it is the only option that gives a single, player-visible integer both rule engines (`anchor_sim.gd`, `sim/engine.py`) can enforce identically. See PLC-05 and the DECISIONS.md entry it added.

lane.description: index into the anchor's `paths` array. Defaults to 0, so an anchor with a single lane needs no `lane` key on any spawn.

tutorial.description: relaxes the multiple-viable-builds requirement. Only legitimate while few emplacements are unlocked.

capacity_decay_mw.description: Act III: MW the bus loses at the start of each wave after the first, floored at 45% of rated capacity.

lane_half_width.description: PLC-02. Half-width, in tiles, of the standoff the free-placement legality predicate keeps between an emplacement's footprint and the path polyline: a position is legal off-lane only where its squared distance to the nearest lane segment is at least (lane_half_width + footprint_radius)^2. Defaults to 0.5 (today's single-tile lane) so every anchor that omits this key resolves to the same standoff the fixed-slot game always had. Authored per anchor so a level can widen its road.

terrain.description: Optional; absent means the whole board is level 0. Regions, not a dense heightmap, are the normal way to author relief: they are what a generator emits and what a human can read in a diff. Resolution algorithm (implemented twice, byte for byte, by sim/content.py's resolve_terrain() and scripts/content.gd's resolve_terrain(), and proved identical on data/schema/fixtures/terrain-resolution.json by the 'terrain parsers agree' gate check -- PRD-THEATRE-SCALE.md risk #10 is exactly these two parsers disagreeing on this one algorithm): if `heightmap` is present it REPLACES `regions` entirely and is never composited with them, which is why declaring both is a schema error (the `not` clause above) rather than a silent precedence rule. Otherwise every tile starts at level 0 and `regions` are painted in array order -- a later region's `rect` completely overwrites the level of every tile it covers, including lowering it below what an earlier region wrote. Later region wins, full stop, and that is the entire rule. `ramps` are declared, not inferred, and are metadata for a future line-of-sight / stepped-movement consumer -- they are not consulted by this resolution algorithm and do not affect the resolved grid.

levels.description: the maximum level index the board uses; every region/heightmap z must satisfy 0 <= z <= levels.

rect.description: [x, y, w, h]; half-open in w and h.

heightmap.description: dense h x w array of integer levels, row-major: heightmap[y][x]. Replaces `regions` entirely when present; declaring both is a schema error.
